title: CXL-INTERPLAY: Unraveling and Characterizing CXL Interference in Modern Computer Systems
problem: Compute Express Link (CXL) enables memory/storage expansion but faces performance degradation when coexisting with conventional memory and storage systems; interference effects are largely unexplored in real hardware, creating blind spots in deployment.
motivation: CXL adoption is growing but under-characterized interference patterns limit confidence in heterogeneous memory system designs; systematic characterization on real hardware is essential for practical deployment.
method: CXL-Interplay investigates how conventional memory and storage systems slow down CXL (Compute Express Link, a standard for memory and storage expansion) by testing on real CXL hardware. The team measures CPU performance metrics and monitors operating-system-level activity to reverse-engineer the specific resource conflicts causing slowdowns. They then test and evaluate solutions that reduce these interference effects.
key_novelty: CXL-Interplay is the first systematic characterization of Compute Express Link (a standard for memory and storage expansion) interference on real hardware and the first to reverse-engineer the interference mechanisms using performance metrics.
contributions: First CXL interference characterization on real hardware
Performance counter and kernel-level reverse-reasoning analysis
limitations: Characterization limited to specific CXL hardware; generalization to different CXL implementations and broader system configurations not discussed.
